exposure: Prenatal employment status (full-time employment, not employed)
cohort: Nationally representative sample of women who gave birth in U.S. hospitals (n = 1,573)
finding: Full-time prenatal employment is associated with higher odds of cesarean delivery, but this association was not explained by socioeconomic status and no longer existed after accounting for sociodemographic differences by matching women employed full time with similar women not employed during pregnancy.
